instruction: Ensure that all regular files in the present directory and its subfolders have permissions set to 666.

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.write('cd testDir'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.press('enter'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.write('clear'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.press('enter')

include: All files have the correct permissions.

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing all file permissions to 666 (rw-rw-rw-) which allows all users to read and write. The setup creates files with permissions 755, 644, and 777. The evaluator runs eval_2.sh which verifies all files have 666 permissions. This is similar in complexity to the original task.

Permission check is semantically correct: compares ls -l output against '-rw-rw-rw-' which is the string representation of 666 permissions
